title: Basic Investment Terms
blurb: The investment words clients actually ask about, explained in plain language with numbers.

rows: New employees (all sections), sales team (talk-tracks, role-plays, niche topics); investors as awareness material
About 89 minutes of lessons, plus role-play and the final quiz
Each L.E.A.R.N. stage has: what to know, how to do it, a talk-track, and the investor takeaway

sources: SEBI Master Circular for Mutual Funds (current edition)

lessons.title: What a fund is: pool, AMC, scheme, units, NAV, AUM
Plans and options: direct, regular, growth, IDCW, folio, NFO
Labels that matter: open-ended, benchmark, TRI, categories, index funds
Measuring the bumps: volatility, beta, Sharpe, Sortino, drawdown
Building the mix: allocation, diversification, liquidity, emergency fund
Putting money in: lump sum, SIP, STP, SWP, switch, redemption
Paperwork and timing: KYC, nomination, cut-off, exit load, lock-in, TER
Costs and documents: stamp duty, ELSS, SID/KIM, factsheet, CAS
Returns done right: absolute, CAGR, XIRR, trailing, rolling
Judging performance: alpha, tracking error, overlap, rebalancing, Rule of 72
Markets and moods: bull, bear, correction, timing, compounding
Inflation and behaviour: real return, paper loss, recency bias, FOMO
Debt terms (2): credit quality and strategy
Compliance: dos, don'ts and the final check

a: Price of one unit = (value of holdings − expenses) ÷ units. Declared once every business day.
Assets Under Management: the total money a fund or AMC manages.
Your account number with an AMC. Quote it for any service request.
Same portfolio and manager. Regular includes distributor commission (for advice and service) in its expense ratio.
Benchmark version that includes dividends; the fair yardstick SEBI requires funds to compare against.
SEBI's six levels: Low, Low to Moderate, Moderate, Moderately High, High, Very High.
3 pm for most funds; 1:30 pm for liquid and overnight funds. Money received after it gets the next day's NAV.
0.005% on mutual fund purchases: ₹50 on ₹10 lakh.
3 years, counted separately for each SIP instalment.
One-time identity and address verification, recorded with a KYC Registration Agency.
Consolidated Account Statement: all your mutual fund holdings across AMCs in one statement.
72 ÷ yearly return = years to double. At 12%, about 6 years.
Return after inflation. 7% FD with 6% inflation ≈ 1% real, before tax.
Correction: a fall of about 10–20% from a peak. Bear market: about 20% or more.
An agency's grade of a borrower's ability to repay. AAA is highest; below BBB− is below investment grade.
Scheme Information Document / Key Information Memorandum: the official offer documents to read before investing.
Growth keeps profits invested; IDCW pays out of the investor's own capital and gains.
Example: ₹1 per unit paid → NAV falls by ₹1
Remember: IDCW is not extra income.
A fixed amount invested automatically at regular intervals, from bank to fund.
Example: ₹10,000 on the 5th of every month
Remember: Buys more units when prices are low.
Money moved in instalments from one fund to another, usually debt to equity.
Example: ₹12 L in a liquid fund, ₹1 L a month to equity
Remember: Fund to fund, not bank to fund.
A fixed amount withdrawn regularly from a fund to the bank.
Example: Retiree takes ₹40,000 a month
Remember: You choose the amount and date.
Exit load: you can leave early but pay a fee. Lock-in: you cannot leave at all.
Example: e.g. 1% within a year vs ELSS 3 years
Remember: Check each scheme's SID.
Yearly cost of running the fund, taken daily from the NAV; capped by SEBI.
Example: 1.5% vs 0.5% on ₹10 L over 20 yrs ≈ ₹14.5 L gap (illustrative)
Remember: Show costs in rupees.
Absolute ignores time; CAGR is the steady yearly rate.
Example: ₹1 L → ₹2 L in 5 yrs = 100% absolute ≈ 14.9% CAGR
Remember: 100% in 5 years is not 20% a year.
Annualised return when money goes in or out on different dates.
Example: The right measure for SIPs
Remember: CAGR for lump sums, XIRR for SIPs.
A number for how much returns swing around their average.
Example: SD 20% is bumpier than SD 12%
Remember: Higher = bigger swings.
How much a fund moves compared with its benchmark.
Example: Beta 1.2: market moves 10%, fund ~12%
Remember: Above 1 = more sensitive than the market.
Return above the risk-free rate per unit of volatility.
Example: Same return, higher Sharpe = smoother ride
Remember: Higher is better.
Fall from a peak to a low before recovering.
Example: ₹10 L falls to ₹7 L = 30% drawdown
Remember: Can the client sit through it?
How much a debt fund's price changes for a 1% change in interest rates.
Example: Duration 4: rates up 1% → price ≈ −4%
Remember: Match duration to the goal date.
Yield to Maturity: the indicative return of the fund's bonds if held to maturity, before expenses.
Example: YTM 7.4%, TER 0.4% → ~7% indicative
Remember: A guide, not a promise.
Earning returns on past returns, so growth speeds up over time.
Example: ₹10,000/month for 20 yrs at 12% ≈ ₹1 Cr on ₹24 L (illustrative)
Remember: Time matters more than timing.
A fixed SIP buys more units when prices are low and fewer when high.
Example: ₹10,000 buys 200 units at ₹50, 250 at ₹40
Remember: Falls help a SIP investor.

questions.q: NAV stands for:
questions.why: Net Asset Value. It is the price of one unit of a fund.

questions.q: Fund A has NAV ₹10 and Fund B has NAV ₹200. Which is cheaper?
o: Neither; NAV level doesn't make a fund cheap
questions.why: Neither; NAV level doesn't make a fund cheap. Returns depend on how much the NAV grows, not where it starts.

questions.q: Which return measure suits a SIP?
questions.why: XIRR. XIRR handles money invested on different dates.

questions.q: ₹1 lakh grows to ₹2 lakh in 5 years. The CAGR is about:
When an IDCW of ₹1 per unit is paid, the NAV:
questions.why: Falls by ₹1. The payout comes out of the fund's assets.

questions.q: The ELSS lock-in is:
questions.why: 3 years. Counted separately for each SIP instalment.

questions.q: Money moved monthly from a liquid fund into an equity fund is a:
questions.why: STP. STP moves money fund to fund.

questions.q: TER is:
o: The yearly cost of running the fund
questions.why: The yearly cost of running the fund. Charged daily through the NAV.

questions.q: Stamp duty on mutual fund purchases is:
The cut-off time for most equity funds is:
questions.why: 3 pm. Liquid and overnight funds: 1:30 pm.

questions.q: A beta of 1.2 means the fund tends to move:
questions.why: About 20% more than the market. Beta above 1 = more sensitive than the market.

questions.q: How many levels does the SEBI riskometer have?
questions.why: 6. Low to Very High.

questions.q: A debt fund with modified duration 5 will, if rates rise 1%, roughly:
questions.why: Lose 5%. Modified duration × rate change ≈ price change.

questions.q: With 6% inflation, a 7% FD gives a real return of about:
questions.why: 1%. Before tax.

questions.q: Using the Rule of 72, money growing at 12% doubles in about:
How do an exit load and a lock-in differ?
o: An exit load is a fee for leaving early; a lock-in blocks exit entirely
A lock-in is a fee; an exit load blocks exit
questions.why: Exit load is a fee for leaving early; a lock-in blocks exit entirely.

questions.q: A debt fund shows a high YTM. What does that guarantee?
o: The return, if held to maturity
Nothing — YTM is indicative; rate moves and credit events can change returns
questions.why: YTM is indicative; prices and credit can change.

questions.q: Direct and regular plans of a scheme differ in:
o: Only the expense ratio, which includes distributor commission in the regular plan
questions.why: The difference is the expense ratio, which includes distributor commission in the regular plan.

questions.q: A client holds five large-cap funds. Why might that not be diversification?
o: They may hold mostly the same stocks; check portfolio overlap
Five funds is too few by rule
questions.why: They may hold mostly the same stocks; check portfolio overlap.

questions.q: What is real return?
questions.why: Nominal return minus inflation, roughly.

questions.q: A client says, “This NFO is only ₹10, so it’s cheaper than the fund at ₹200.” What do you explain?
o: Agree — a lower NAV is always cheaper
NAV is the price of one unit; the same % growth gives the same rupee result, so judge by strategy, cost and fit, not NAV level
That NFOs are banned for new investors
questions.why: Explains NAV as a price per unit; same % growth gives the same rupee result; judges by strategy, cost and fit, not NAV level.

questions.q: A client’s SIP statement shows 45% after 3 years and they think that is 15% a year. What do you explain?
o: That 45% divided by 3 is the right yearly return
Absolute return ignores time; for a SIP the right annualised measure is XIRR, compared with the TRI benchmark
That SIP returns are never annualised
That only CAGR applies to SIPs
questions.why: Explains absolute vs annualised return; shows XIRR as the right measure; compares with TRI benchmark.

questions.q: A retiree wants the IDCW option “for monthly income”. What do you explain?
o: That IDCW is guaranteed monthly income
IDCW is paid from own capital, amount and timing not fixed; compare SWP for a chosen, regular amount; tax via CA
questions.why: IDCW is paid from own capital, amount and timing not fixed; compares SWP for a chosen, regular amount; tax via CA.

questions.q: A client’s debt fund fell 2% in a month and they say, “I thought debt was safe.” How do you respond?
o: Promise it will recover next month
Explain interest-rate risk and duration (and credit risk if relevant); check duration vs goal date; no promise of recovery
questions.why: Explains interest-rate risk and duration (and credit risk if relevant); checks duration vs goal date; no promise of recovery.

questions.q: A client placed a ₹5 lakh purchase at 2:50 pm, but the money reached the AMC at 3:20 pm, so they got the next day’s NAV. Why?
o: Cut-off is 3 pm (1:30 pm for liquid); for purchases the NAV depends on when money is received by the AMC, not when the form was submitted
Purchases always get the next day’s NAV
questions.why: Explains cut-off time (3 pm; 1:30 pm for liquid) and that for purchases the NAV depends on when the money is received by the AMC, not when the form was submitted.
